clue.text: One could look through this for place to study at Oxford

definitions.meaning: a window, here a bay window projecting from an upper floor
one of the colleges of Oxford University bears this name

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a projecting upper-storey window and an Oxford college, so each half of the clue is a separate sense.

clue.text: Bad woman pinching article that's ready to wear

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip, so the outer pieces hold the article between them

parts.note: food gone bad is off
Peg is a woman's name
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A wicked woman steals an item of clothing that is ready to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes bought ready-made in standard sizes, rather than tailored, are ready to wear.

clue.text: Order given somewhat histrionically

indicators.note: somewhat means a part of, so the answer is a part of the following word

explanation.surface: A command is delivered rather theatrically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command; it is a classical order of architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the classical orders of architecture, with scroll-shaped capitals.

clue.text: Work over for work-shy type

definitions.meaning: to attack or beat someone, to set about them
an idle person who avoids work

explanation.definitionFit: Split as a phrasal verb, it means to attack; as a noun, it means a lazy idler.

clue.text: Why Enigma novel was a bestseller

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new or fresh, so the letters of the two words before it are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone explains why a novel about the wartime Enigma code sold so well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book in question but is the anagram signal working on WHY ENIGMA.
explanation.definitionFit: The American author of The Old Man and the Sea was a hugely popular writer, so a bestselling novelist stands for him.

clue.text: Laugh, or sound warning

definitions.meaning: an outburst of laughter, or something very funny
to blow a car horn as a warning

explanation.definitionFit: It means both a burst of laughter and the noise of a horn sounded as a warning.

clue.text: At sea, a man tasked to resist attack

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor at sea is given orders to fight off an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' looks like the setting for the man, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a stand is to hold one's ground and resist an attack.

clue.text: Picked up kill speared by jolly skilful hunter

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the letters read upwards, in reverse
the kill is pierced by the jolly, which goes inside it

parts.note: to do in is to kill
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: A hunter's lifted prey is speared by a cheerful, expert stalker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speared by' gives DORMIN, which 'Picked up' turns round. 'jolly' looks like cheerful, but it is slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this figure is called a mighty hunter, so the name stands for any skilled hunter.

clue.text: What's now being diverted round a lake?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the other piece
diverted means rerouted, so the letters are sent along a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller asks what is now being rerouted around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' rearranges NOW BEING to WINNEBGO, which goes 'round' A. Lake Winnebago is in Wisconsin; the word is also a motorhome brand that might take a diversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Winnebago is the largest lake wholly in the US state of Wisconsin.

clue.text: Makes special deliveries in the county

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to bowl a yorker, a ball pitched at the batsman's feet
an abbreviation for Yorkshire, England's largest county

explanation.definitionFit: A bowler who bowls a yorker is said to york the batsman; it is also the short form of Yorkshire.

clue.text: Go for a job in embroidery

parts.note: to go for someone or something is to fancy them
a job is a piece of work

explanation.surface: Someone decides to apply for a position in a needlework business.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental needlework such as embroidery is traditionally called by this compound word.

clue.text: So-called fashion house

indicators.note: so-called here means called out or spoken, so the word is one that is heard rather than written

parts.note: a fashion is a way or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: A grandly named fashion house is mocked as only 'so-called'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion house' reads as one phrase, but 'fashion' gives the sound and 'house' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A country estate's principal residence is a large house, often the lord's house.

clue.text: Queen's ambassador going to foreign country

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the clue says the queen is what follows

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the formal title of an ambassador
Cuba is a Caribbean island nation

explanation.surface: A British envoy representing the monarch is posted to a country abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Britain's Queen; the answer is the queen of Troy in Greek legend, wife of Priam.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer and Greek tragedy she is the wife of King Priam, making her the queen of Troy.

clue.text: Lady perhaps seen in singles bars, hanging around

indicators.note: the word bars hangs around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
singles are ones, single units

explanation.surface: A titled woman is spotted lurking in singles bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singles bars' reads as one phrase, but 'singles' is the piece that 'hanging around' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness is entitled to be called Lady, so a Lady is an example, as 'perhaps' signals.

clue.text: Seeming to be in less trouble

indicators.note: trouble means disturb, so the preceding letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone appears to be less troubled than before.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means apparent or as it seems, not necessarily real.

clue.text: Mistakenly queries tip, but it's an incidental benefit

indicators.note: letters set down mistakenly are out of order, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly questions a gratuity, though it is just a perk of the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk is a benefit received alongside one's salary, an incidental extra of employment.

clue.text: Salesman disheartened competitor in sorry state

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: an entrant is a competitor

explanation.surface: A salesman demoralises a rival who is left in a pitiful condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle letter R of ENTRANT, leaving ENTANT. 'sorry' means regretful, not wretched.
explanation.definitionFit: A repentant person is sorry for what they did, in a state of regret.

clue.text: Fire didn't start in lounge

indicators.note: the word for fire loses its opening letter, so it does not start as usual

parts.note: a blaze is a fire

explanation.surface: A fire in a sitting room failed to catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' looks like a room where the fire would be, but it is a verb meaning to idle.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to relax lazily, which is also what to laze means.

clue.text: Very sociable party animal in former times?

definitions.meaning: an outgoing person, in the spelling Jung used before the usual modern one

explanation.definitionFit: This older spelling of the word for an outgoing person serves as adjective and as noun for a party lover.

clue.text: Given higher position, you finally cracked up

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word you

parts.note: to be cracked up is to be praised highly

explanation.surface: Someone promoted is told that they finally went to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked up' suggests a breakdown, but it means praised, as in 'not all it's cracked up to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Upraised means lifted up, raised to a higher position.

clue.text: One small opening close to one wide opening

parts.note: a gap is a small opening

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here taken from the second one

explanation.surface: A tiny aperture sits next to a large one.
explanation.definitionFit: A gape is a wide opening, as of a mouth or beak opened wide.

clue.text: The head has spring vegetable

parts.note: bean is slang for the head
to spring up is to sprout

explanation.surface: Someone's head boasts a fresh spring vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring vegetable' reads as one phrase, but 'spring' is a verb giving SPROUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Germinated mung beans, eaten as a crisp vegetable, are known by this name.

clue.text: Fool wearing jacket with no sleeves or collar

definitions.text: jacket with no sleeves or collar

parts.note: a jerk is a fool
if you are in something, you are wearing it

explanation.surface: A fool sports a sleeveless, collarless jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a close-fitting, often sleeveless jacket, traditionally of leather.

clue.text: Turned round to have a chat

definitions.meaning: the reverse or opposite of something, as in a statement turned round

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means reversed or opposite; as a verb it means to talk together, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Island resort in better state

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: An island holiday spot is in improved condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better state' reads as an improved condition; 'better' is a verb giving CAP and 'state' gives RI.
explanation.definitionFit: An island in the Bay of Naples, famous as a holiday resort.

clue.text: Dish almost everyone's bound to return

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the assembled letters are read backwards
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: everyone is all
a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: Nearly everybody is obliged to come back for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ALL to AL; AL plus LEAP gives ALLEAP, and 'return' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish rice dish with seafood or meat cooked in a wide pan.

clue.text: Deposit for holiday

definitions.meaning: to put down or ... something somewhere

explanation.definitionFit: It means both to deposit or leave behind something and an official holiday from work.

clue.text: Nasty cold king's caught

indicators.note: the cold word catches the king, holding it inside

parts.note: icy means very cold
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A nasty cold has been caught by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Icky is informal for unpleasant or nasty, especially sticky or distasteful.

clue.text: Board considered item in political party's programme

definitions.meaning: a long flat piece of timber

definitions.text: considered item in political party's programme
definitions.meaning: one policy point in a party's platform

explanation.definitionFit: A wooden board, and figuratively one policy item in a party platform, extending the platform image.

clue.text: Second room key used to find character already in?

definitions.text: key used to find character already in?

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
room means space

explanation.surface: A second room's key is used to look for a person already inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a door key and a person; it is a keyboard key returning to a character already typed.
explanation.definitionFit: The keyboard key that steps back over typed characters, letting you reach one already entered.

clue.text: Extremely popular figure fans finally get to see

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
ten is a number or figure

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word fans

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely in Cambridgeshire is one

explanation.surface: A hugely popular celebrity's fans at last get to see the star.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something intensely means doing it to an extreme degree.

clue.text: Remained dependable when everyone lost their heads

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, taken from each of the five words before

explanation.surface: Someone stayed reliable while all around were losing their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Kipling's 'If': keeping your head when all about you are losing theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live or stay there, so dwelt means stayed or remained.
